theHEADLINE: NEITHER FAMILY REPRODUCED ANY OF THE FIVE DISPATCHED FINDINGS. All five were closed before this lane existed -- four by FIX165 at 6abfa62a1 and de1e451c6, the fifth by the Captain's shared-record sweep -- and each was re-derived here from the delivered bytes and the committed records at HEAD before anything was touched. No repair was manufactured for any of them. howBytesWereMeasured.pixels: pdftoppm -r 300 -gray writing binary P5 PGM, read by a P5 reader written for this lane; never -png. Ink threshold grey < 128 of 255. Per-control counts are added ink: a pixel is counted only where the delivered page is inked and the pinned source page at the same coordinate is not.
howBytesWereMeasured.positiveControlBeforeEveryZero: Every zero reported below was read in the SAME RUN as a positive control on the SAME page with the SAME detector. At paragraphs 9 and 10 the control is paragraphs 1, 2 and 8 on the same two pages, which read 1,927, 2,100 and 88 px while all four paragraph 9/10 boxes read 0.
howBytesWereMeasured.glyphs: Flattened widget Form XObjects located through each page's /XObject resource dictionary and decompressed with pdf-lib's decodePDFRawStream. An appearance counts as inked only when its stream carries a Tj/TJ operator AND its show-text operands hold at least one non-whitespace character.
howBytesWereMeasured.nonGlyphInk: Flattened widget appearances carrying a paint operator (S s f F f* B B* b b*) and NO Tj/TJ. Added because a check-box election on these ACIC forms flattens to a painted mark, not to text, and every glyph figure is structurally blind to it.
howBytesWereMeasured.text: pdftotext, run in -layout, -raw and default reading order, because the default order interleaves a two-column caption and the -raw order fuses a hyphenated line break. A quoted line counts as verified if it matches under any of the three; two apparent misquotes were extraction artefacts of a single mode and are recorded under whatDIDNOTREPRODUCE.
howBytesWereMeasured.digests: sha256sum on the files on disk, before and after every build.
howBytesWereMeasured.recordAnchors: JSON canonicalised as keys sorted recursively, no separators, UTF-8 WITHOUT ASCII escaping, then sha256. The escaping matters: Python's default ensure_ascii=True escapes the section sign in these records and produces a different digest from the JS mechanism, which is why this lane's first anchor comparison disagreed with the receipt before it was corrected.

sideEffectsFound.what: Every run drops the line "acceptanceReceipt": null. writeWiring builds the object with `acceptanceReceipt: undefined` to reserve the committed key order, and JSON.stringify omits an undefined value, so the key the committed tree carries as an explicit null cannot survive a rebuild. The committed tree is therefore not reproducible from the builder for this one file, by one line.

sideEffectsFound.what: NOT a side effect of a successful build, but a real fragility this lane triggered and is recording. runFamily calls fs.rmSync on the whole output directory before rebuilding, and the identityRefresh evidence block is carried forward from the receipt it finds on disk. A build that CRASHES after the rmSync leaves no receipt, and the NEXT successful build then ships a receipt with the identity-refresh justification silently stripped -- a fresh-looking pin with the evidence removed. This is exactly the hazard VF57 named as its reason for not running the builder, reached by a different route. It happened once here during guard-break testing.
sideEffectsFound.handling: Restored from git and rebuilt; the block is carried forward correctly when the prior receipt is present, verified. Not in either commit. Reported for the Captain because it makes every crashed build a potential silent evidence loss across the corpus, not just here.
